design_summary: One continuous mountain with a horizontal granite-limestone contact at Y=200. No V-shaped ravine. Composite terrane plaque moved to the service tunnel contact crossing. Return route is funicular + summit road (no skybridge). New 7th centerpiece: summit observation platform at Y=800.

renderings.title: Combined Complex Overview (No-Ravine)
renderings.subject: Wide aerial panorama of the complete world showing one continuous mountain, horizontal contact at Y=200, city, and coastal plain
renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: Removed V-shaped ravine; one continuous mountain with horizontal contact visible as color line; removed skybridge from return route; summit observation platform visible at peak
renderings.intended_use: Master plan cover image; the single most important hero shot of the entire project

renderings.title: 4-Layer Defense-in-Depth Cross-Section
renderings.subject: Signature cross-section showing all 4 layers: civilian surface, climate-controlled shallow, industrial limestone, military granite, with ascending service tunnel crossing the contact at Y=200
renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: Service tunnel is now ASCENDING through the mountain, crossing the horizontal contact at Y=200 (was a horizontal bore under a ravine)
renderings.intended_use: Defense-in-depth chapter hero; the build's visual signature

renderings.title: Continuous Mountain Range (No Ravine)
renderings.subject: Wide exterior shot of ONE continuous mountain range with a horizontal granite-limestone contact at Y=200, no V-notch, no gorge
renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: Renamed from 03-mountain-range-ravine.png; removed the V-shaped ravine; added the horizontal contact line as the mountain's signature
renderings.intended_use: Mountain range chapter hero; establishes the silhouette of the no-ravine design

renderings.title: Composite Terrane Plaque at Service Tunnel Contact Crossing (Close-up)
renderings.subject: Close-up of the 1x2 carved-stone composite terrane plaque in a 3x5 alcove in the service tunnel at the contact crossing
renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: Plaque MOVED from the ravine bottom (now deleted) to the service tunnel contact crossing, where the wall material visibly transitions from limestone to granite. Geologically honest: real granite plutons push up through limestone in mountain ranges worldwide.
renderings.intended_use: The build's Telling Detail; the geological premise made honest by placing the plaque where the contact actually is

renderings.title: City in the Valley (with Continuous Mountain Backdrop)
renderings.subject: Houston-style city in a wide flat valley with 4 anchor towers, glass skybridges, T-markers, and a continuous mountain rising behind with a horizontal contact line
renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: Mountain backdrop is now one continuous mass with a horizontal contact line (no V-notch ravine in the background)
renderings.intended_use: City in the valley chapter hero; the civilian anchor of the build

renderings.title: Public Shaft Surface Pavilion

renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: Pavilion location unchanged; still at the city surface, vertical descent through limestone
renderings.intended_use: Public shaft chapter hero; the first surface entrance the player encounters

renderings.title: Public Shaft Descent
renderings.subject: 5x5 mechanical lift descending through a 7x7 vertical shaft with iron-bars enclosure, visible emergency stair, and wall material transitions
renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: Unchanged; the public shaft is a vertical descent through limestone that does not depend on the surface ravine
renderings.intended_use: Public shaft descent sequence; the 'you are descending' feel

renderings.title: Public Shaft Mid-Level Observation Landing
renderings.subject: 7x7 observation landing at Y=-50 with a G-Cans-style glass window to a utility corridor, oak bench, information sign, and labelled limestone block
renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: Unchanged
renderings.intended_use: Centerpiece #2 (non-negotiable); the G-Cans moment; the breath between the two halves of the descent

renderings.title: Public Shaft SubTropolis Public Access Lobby
renderings.subject: 7x7 lobby at Y=-100 with security gate, turnstile, dual-use sign, Helsinki 5,500 reference, and door opening onto the SubTropolis chamber
renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: Unchanged
renderings.intended_use: Public shaft termination; the arrival moment; Easter egg #4

renderings.title: Service Tunnel Limestone Section
renderings.subject: 6x6 service tunnel in cream-grey limestone with minecart rail, SubTropolis color-coded utility strip, and yellow emergency-escape corridor
renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: Renamed from 10-service-tunnel-subtropolis-entry.png; old SubTropolis entry image rolled into the 4-layer cross-section; the new file 10 is the limestone section of the ascending service tunnel
renderings.intended_use: Service tunnel interior, SubTropolis aesthetic; the 'creamer, working, industrial' feel

renderings.title: Service Tunnel Contact Crossing (Geological Moment)
renderings.subject: 6x6 service tunnel at the horizontal granite-limestone contact crossing, with walls transitioning from calcite to polished diorite, 1-block breccia strip, and the composite terrane plaque in its 3x5 alcove
renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: Renamed from 12-service-tunnel-thrust-fault.png. Was at the ravine bottom (now deleted); now at the actual geological contact inside the ascending service tunnel. The signature interior shot of the build.
renderings.intended_use: The 'you are traveling through 800 million years of geology' moment; the build's geological spine

renderings.title: Service Tunnel Granite Section
renderings.subject: 6x6 service tunnel in pink-grey polished diorite granite with self-supporting ceiling, minecart rail, Cheyenne color-coded utilities (gray, black, red), and visible 4:1 grade ascending toward the blast door
renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: Same name, new content; the granite section of the ascending service tunnel replaces the previous (ravine-era) flat granite section
renderings.intended_use: Service tunnel interior, Cheyenne aesthetic; the regime change from civilian to military made visible through color-coded utilities

renderings.title: Service Tunnel 25-Ton Blast Door (Cheyenne Outer Portal at Y=200)
renderings.subject: 3-block-thick iron blast door in a quartz-stair frame at the end of the service tunnel at Y=200, with checkpoint corridor, guard booth, and U.S. Space Force / Authorized Personnel Only sign

renderings.intended_use: Centerpiece #1 (non-negotiable); the architectural climax of the service tunnel; the cinematic moment of arriving at Cheyenne

renderings.title: Cheyenne Portal from Outside (Y=200, Granite Face)
renderings.subject: Wide exterior shot of the Cheyenne portal in the pink-grey granite mountain face at Y=200, with security perimeter, antenna arrays, snow line, and horizontal contact visible as a color line on the mountain
renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: Same name, new content; the portal is now on the continuous mountain's granite face (was on the granite north wall of the V-ravine)
renderings.intended_use: Architectural object #6; the exterior face of the Cheyenne end

renderings.title: SubTropolis Portal from Outside (South Face of Continuous Mountain)
renderings.subject: Wide exterior shot of the SubTropolis horizontal portal carved into the cream limestone flank of the continuous mountain, with paved road switchback, parking lot, oak forest, and horizontal contact above as a color line
renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: Same name, new content; the portal is now on the continuous mountain's limestone flank (was on the limestone south wall of the V-ravine)
renderings.intended_use: Architectural object #5; the drive-in face of the SubTropolis end; Easter egg #5

renderings.title: Houston Tunnel Entrances
renderings.subject: Street-level view of Wells Fargo Plaza and McKinney Garage Houston tunnel entrances with T-markers, glass skybridges, and a glimpse into the dim tunnel below
renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: Unchanged
renderings.intended_use: Houston tunnel chapter; Easter egg #7 (T-markers)

renderings.title: Coastal Plain Edge (with Continuous Mountain in the Distance)
renderings.subject: Coastal plain extending to the world edge with arrival road, sparse forest, lake, dock, and the city/continuous-mountain backdrop with horizontal contact visible
renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: Same name, new content; the mountain backdrop is now one continuous mass (no V-notch)
renderings.intended_use: The 'you've reached the edge of the build' moment; frames the build

renderings.title: Full Visitor Journey Cross-Section (No-Ravine)
renderings.subject: Full visitor journey from city surface to deep granite chambers and back: city surface, Houston tunnel, public shaft with mid-landing, SubTropolis, ASCENDING service tunnel crossing the contact at Y=200, Cheyenne chamber, funicular to summit, summit road back. NO skybridge.
renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: Service tunnel is now an ASCENDING minecart bore through the mountain, not a horizontal bore under a ravine. Return is funicular + summit road, no skybridge. Summit observation platform at Y=800 is the new payoff of the return route.
renderings.intended_use: The 'single trajectory' hero shot; the build's narrative compressed into one image

renderings.title: Funicular + Summit Road Return (No Skybridge)
renderings.subject: Funicular car on a 1-block-wide powered rail descending the granite face from the summit station at Y=800 to the Cheyenne outer portal at Y=200 (2:1 gradient), plus a 6-block-wide stone-brick road switchbacking down the south face to the city. NO skybridge.
renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: Same name, new content; skybridge removed. The return is funicular + summit road, with the new summit observation platform at Y=800 as the narrative payoff.
renderings.intended_use: The return journey; the 2-mode return replaces the previous design's skybridge

renderings.title: Summit Observation Platform at Y=800 (7th Centerpiece, NEW)
renderings.subject: New 7th centerpiece: a small 10x10 oak-plank platform with a spruce-fence railing at Y=800, a Three Sites, One Mountain sign, and a 360-degree panoramic view of the continuous mountain, the city, the coastal plain
renderings.design_change_vs_ravine: NEW. The previous ravine design had no summit platform (the skybridge was the return-route payoff). The no-ravine design adds a summit observation platform as the 7th centerpiece, with a 'Three Sites, One Mountain' sign.
renderings.intended_use: The 7th centerpiece (new in the no-ravine design); the narrative payoff of the return route

renderings.title: Gotthard-Inspired Service Tunnel Sign (with Record Holder Named)

renderings.title: Thrust-Fault Breccia Strip in Service Tunnel Floor (Close-up)
renderings.subject: 1-block-wide strip of mixed cobblestone and calcite breccia in the service tunnel floor at the contact crossing, surrounded by limestone and granite

renderings.intended_use: Easter egg #8 (thrust-fault breccia strip detail); the companion detail to the contact-crossing alcove (rendering #11)

renderings.title: Rock Identification Chart at Granite Summit
renderings.subject: 3-block display chart at the granite summit with labelled samples of Pikes Peak granite, Bethany Falls limestone, and thrust-fault breccia

summary.previous_revision_removed: ravine (V-shaped gorge with composite terrane at the ravine bottom)
key_design_changes: Mountain layout: ONE continuous mass (was: V-shaped ravine splitting two peaks)
Geology: horizontal granite-limestone contact at Y=200 (was: composite terrane thrust fault at the ravine bottom)
Composite terrane plaque: inside the service tunnel at the contact crossing (was: at the ravine bottom)
Service tunnel: ascending minecart bore through the mountain (was: horizontal bore under the ravine)
Return route: funicular + summit road (was: funicular + skybridge + road)
New 7th centerpiece: summit observation platform at Y=800 (replaces skybridge as return-route payoff)
block_palette_used: cobblestone (thrust-fault breccia in the service tunnel floor)
snow-layer (peak summit, snow line at Y=700)
